questions.question: What does the `throw` keyword do in Java?
options: Declares that a method can throw an exception
Throws an exception explicitly in the code
Catches an exception that has already been thrown
Ignores an exception and continues execution
explanations: Declaring exceptions is the job of throws, not throw.
Correct. The throw keyword is used to throw (instantiate and send) an exception explicitly in the code.
Catching exceptions is the job of the catch block, not throw.
throw does not ignore exceptions; it actively throws them.

questions.question: What does the `throws` keyword indicate in a method signature?
options: That the method always throws an exception
That the method can throw that exception and the caller must handle it
That the method automatically catches all exceptions
That the method cannot throw exceptions of any kind
explanations: throws does not mean the method always throws exceptions; it indicates it is possible.
Correct. throws declares in the method signature that the method may throw a specific exception, and the code calling the method must handle it or propagate it.
throws does not catch exceptions; it declares them.
throws indicates the possibility of exceptions, not the opposite.

questions.question: When is it appropriate to use throw in the code?
options: In every method that uses String variables
When an invalid condition or an incorrect state is detected in the program
Only when working with text files
Always at the start of each method to prevent errors
explanations: throw has no specific relationship with String variables.
Correct. throw should be used when an invalid condition is detected (null argument, out-of-range value, inconsistent state), indicating that the program cannot continue normally.
throw is not limited to file operations.
Using throw at the start of every method without reason is a bad practice.

questions.question: Is it mandatory to use `throws` in a method signature?
options: Yes, whenever the method can throw a checked exception
Only if the method has more than 3 parameters
Only when working with abstract classes
explanations: throws is mandatory in certain cases, not never.
Correct. For checked exceptions it is mandatory to declare them with throws in the method signature if they are not handled with try-catch inside the method.
The number of parameters does not determine whether throws is needed.
throws has nothing to do with abstract classes.
